newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks end higher, ignore Wall St jitters.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks end higher, ignore Wall St jitters.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed strongly higher on Thursday, managing to shake off Wall Street jitters with some dealers citing a pick-up in consumption.
The general index rose 3.74 points, 0.80 percent, to 469.50 and the Ibex added 46.16 points, 0.87 percent, to 5,357.52.
Gas Natural added 300 pesetas to 31,890 after announcing a 35 percent increase in 1996 net profit.
Repsol meanwhile shed 110 pesetas to 5,450, with the government expected to approve the privatisation calendar shortly for the sale of its last 10 percent stake, expected some time around April.
Corporate results were helping to give the market direction, and some dealers were citing expectations of further rate cuts this year and a recovery in consumption as factors encouraging buyers.
This was reflected by strength in stocks such as hypermarkets Pryca and Continente, they said.
Dealers saw gains continued short-term, as long as there is no substantial fallout from the other side of the Atlantic.
